newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Netanyahu in forex talks with Treasury, Cent Bank.
newsitem.headline: Netanyahu in forex talks with Treasury, Cent Bank.

text.p: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu will meet the country's Finance Minister and the Governor of the Central Bank on Monday in a bid to hammer out a foreign currency liberalisation plan, a government source said.
The discussions are also expected to look at widening the Israeli shekel's trading bands.

The source said that Netanyahu aimed to take a decisive role in a long running dispute between the Treasury and the Central Bank on these two issues. He said he doubted the three would reach a decision tonight but expected a resolution over the next few days.
"We've had numerous discussions about the subject. Both sides have voiced their positions but a decision must be made," Netanyahu told reporters.
The meeting is scheduled for 1700 GMT.
The source said that the absence of any decision had made the local forex markets extremely nervous.

The Bank of Israel, which has been pressing to widen the shekel's currency bands, bought almost $150 million during intervention in the forex market on Monday in an attempt to keep the shekel down, traders said.
The currency is pegged to a basket of foreign currencies and is allowed to trade in a band of seven percent above or below a diagonal line designed to devalue it by six percent a year.
An influx of foreign currency has forced the Bank of Israel to intervene heavily to prevent the shekel from strengthening beyond the seven percent limit.
The Treasury has refused to countenance a widening of the band for fear that it would cause a further appreciation of the shekel, which it regards as being overvalued.
